_about.purpose: Legal, form, and drawing boilerplate that recurs verbatim across construction documents from different projects. Used for two things: rejecting a proposed denylist term during derivation, and suppressing a detector candidate that is entirely boilerplate.
_about.matching: Case-insensitive substring test against the trimmed candidate. Unlike contract_defined_terms.json this is deliberately a containment test, because these phrases arrive with variable surrounding fragments after line wrapping.
_about.scope: Project-independent. Safe to share across every project.

phrases: American Institute of Architects' legal counsel
This document has important legal consequences
Consultation with an attorney is encouraged
Name, legal status and principal place
Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

reject_proposed_term_if._why: Additional structural rules applied to a term proposed by --derive-denylist, on top of the phrase list above.
reject_proposed_term_if._identifier_shape_note: A term that is entirely one of the deterministic identifier patterns (a full street address, a city/state/zip, an email, a URL, a phone number) or a filesystem path is an identifier by construction. Length and prose heuristics are skipped for these, because a real address legitimately runs to eight tokens and a CAD save-path to ten.
reject_proposed_term_if._garbage_note: Extraction garbage from vector text ('rTlfld ifiefti', 'respeKstompletion or', 'Subcontractors, W.._orkby.') shows up as a case flip inside an alphabetic token or as repeated punctuation inside a word. The case-flip test is restricted to pure-ASCII tokens so that mojibake-substituted real names keep proposing.
reject_proposed_term_if._prose_note: A term is prose if it carries two or more function words, or one function word while running to six or more tokens. Tuned so 'City of Panama City, Florida' (five tokens, one function word) survives while 'Treat plywood indicated on Drawings.' (two function words) and 'Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers' (two function words) do not.
